note: The original says his shell came off in a hedge. The rewrite says it got stuck in a hedge and loses the shedding.
last: Big day! Stay put, that's the secret. I didn't, and mine got stuck in a hedge.

note: The original says the house shed. The rewrite says it was stripped and drops the game term shed. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: The house was stripped in spring. We moved into the hollow shell. // The new one is off being a house somewhere else.

note: The original says she caught the hare's cast. The rewrite says she found it and drops the game term catch. Keep the game word catch. It is a term in this game.
last: I found a hare's cast! The real hare is still out there, though. It's much faster than this.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Knuckle always switches when things go south. I don't. I stay loyal.

note: The original says Rib lies west along the Midden Road. The rewrite says to start at Rib and then head west, which changes the direction.
last: Tell the Sealkeepers. Start with Rib, then head west on the Midden Road.

note: The original says the fracture has come right up to the door. The rewrite says trouble has arrived and drops the game term fracture. Keep the game word fracture. It is a term in this game.
last: Tell my little turnip that trouble has finally arrived at the doorstep.

note: The original asks Ouro to move one step over to the side. The rewrite says one step back.
last: Uh, take 1 step back? It's going to come off at an angle.

note: The original says his shell came off late. The rewrite says it came in late.
last: My shell came in late too, and look at him now. Well, don't look at him. He's shy.

note: The original says the whorl picked Ouro back in return. The rewrite says it chose Ouro again.
last: Look at that. It's chosen you again. That bit's on the house.

note: The original jokes that holding the Register costs a cowrie. The rewrite says storage costs a cowrie, which reads as a rule about the Midden.
last: Here's the Register. You catch a species, I log it. Writing is free. Storage costs a cowrie.

note: The original says a weaker whorl makes a surer catch. The rewrite says less strength means better control, which changes the catch rule.
last: Dull them down a bit, then catch them. Less strength means better control. // Weak enough, and it's foolproof.

note: The original prices Knuckle's hands at a house each and calls the pearl cheap. The rewrite prices each pearl at a house and then calls the pearl cheap, which contradicts itself.
last: Start with the Rib. Knuckle holds it steady. Hands-on Knuckle? I'd ask a house per pearl. // The pearl itself is cheap.

note: The original says the Hermits take (seize) big whorls. The rewrite says they bring them.
last: Large whorls can wrench a Seal loose. That's why we bring large whorls.

note: The original says he will go and wait by the well. The rewrite says he will stay where he is.
last: The well stays dry until she returns. I'll stay here and wait.

note: The original means the pearl Knuckle gives out. The rewrite turns the name into a "knuckle-pearl".
last: You've got a knuckle-pearl, right? Then you need one of these.

note: The original notice names Ouro. The rewrite switches to "You acquire", unlike every other notice. Keep the name Ouro.
last: You acquire the prising iron.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Anyway, next stop is Mast. Head west along the Dry Sea.

note: The original hands over the Rib pearl. The rewrite addresses Ouro as "Rib".
last: Here you go, Rib. The pearl is yours.

note: The original says you get tide from the small moves. The rewrite says from "subtle shifts", which no longer names the moves.
last: Crests require tide, right? You gain tide from the subtle shifts. That's the entire mechanism.

note: The original says Tack is still standing in the road. The rewrite invents being caught in a wind shadow.
last: Try {#1}. The count remains 11 Hermits. We're still caught in the wind shadow.

note: The original tells the Hermits to let the Mast lean. The rewrite tells them to let a boat heel.
last: Exhale. Let the boat heel.

note: The original says Leeward's deck is to the north. The rewrite says the deck faces north.
last: Leeward holds the Mast. Leeward's deck faces north.

note: The original says Leeward is one keeper against eleven Hermits. The rewrite says Leeward has one keeper.
last: Leeward has 1 keeper and there are 11 of them. So I'm gonna help. After I beat you.

note: The original greets Ouro as a late one. The rewrite says latecomer, which means someone who arrived late.
last: GREETINGS, latecomer!! Clear skies overhead. Conditions are favorable for a trial.

note: Keep the name Hermits.
last: Hermits' gusts at the base. Thirteen, by the count.

note: The original has nacre caught in the drift. The rewrite says mother-of-pearl and drops the game term nacre. Keep the game word catch, nacre. It is a term in this game.
last: On the distant islet, a pile of driftwood tangled with mother-of-pearl.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: On the western islet, a reed plug trimmed for a bell, left unused.

note: The original says Grandad shed in the nave. The rewrite says he was buried there. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: My grandfather was buried in the nave, // and his cast has been singing the same song there for sixty years.

note: The original means stop the wind-up or take the hit. The rewrite turns it into a threat and loses the battle advice.
last: hear that? yeah, that's a wind-up. cut it out, or you're gonna pay for it.

note: The original has a notion under the acorns. The rewrite says a secret and drops the game term notion. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: Past the sleeping stump in the hollow lies a heap of acorns with a secret hidden beneath them.

note: The original says two nacre. The rewrite says two shells and drops the game term nacre. Keep the game word nacre. It is a term in this game.
last: Beyond the sleeping howl in the dell, two shells wrapped in moss.

note: The original says rain falls upward near the Bole and carries hats up. The rewrite says the rain is strong and loses the upward rain the next line depends on.
last: Keep your hat low near the Bole. The rain there is strong enough to strip it off.

note: The original says Tarhaju whorls drop fruit. The rewrite calls them rings and drops the game term whorl. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: Tarhaju rings bear the same fruit as real orchards. I've sampled plenty myself.

note: The original says Grafton conjoins better than the Conjoiner. The rewrite says Grafton "meshes together" and the second sentence is garbled.
last: Grafton meshes together more smoothly than the Conjoiner does. // Don't tell them either one, or it'll turn into a whole drama.

note: The original says his cast went up into the roots. The rewrite calls it his prosthetic. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: My prosthetic went up into the roots fifty years ago and never came back down. Stubborn creature. // Takes after me, that one.

note: The original says the Grafter made four whorls out of eight and misses two of the originals. The rewrite reads as a score of four out of eight.
last: I got four out of eight. I'm missing two. Which two changes every day.

note: The original says a whorl holds one notion each. The rewrite says the shop has one of each.
last: Oh really? The new notions just arrived. // They're small accessories, but they alter how a whorl approaches combat. I've got one of each.

note: The original calls Ouro a late one. The rewrite says "a slow start".
last: No, no, no. I'm not stopping. Not for a slow start, not for anyone. // We're on a tight schedule, understand?

note: The original says each of Grafton's four was two whorls and is now one. The rewrite says each was once split in two, which reverses it.
last: Every one of my four parts was once split in two. Now, each is singular and magnificent. // (Do not ask which halves.)

note: The original says to fight Grafton's whorls. The rewrite says to activate them.
last: Activate them, and you will witness the doubled magnificence of what two can achieve.

note: The original says the Hermits went north to the machine fields and the town of Hum. The rewrite says Hum went with them.
last: The Hermits moved north into the machine fields, and Hum went with them.

note: The original is about a furnace cast. The rewrite drops cast and says a furnace. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: A furnace stays warm for a century. I sleep right against it. Best sleep of my life.

note: The original says the Pylon is going the way the Bole went. The rewrite says things are going as the Bole intended.
last: Oh, look who it is. Hey. Alright, I'm ahead, you're just getting here. // Things are going exactly as the Bole intended, so...

note: The original says arms in first. The rewrite says arms out first.
last: Arms out first. Then the head. That's it.

note: The letter is signed by Cinch. The rewrite reads the name as the verb "Tighten it". Keep the name Cinch.
last: The Volute must hold. You won't get thanked twice. Tighten it.

note: The original says the Tusk should come out easily. The rewrite says the Hermits should take it easy.
last: We're undermining the Tusk. The oldest one there is. Should take it easy. Probably.

note: The original says his grandmother's grandmother. The rewrite says great-grandmother, which is one generation short.
last: My great-grandmother wore these boots down from the old shell. They're still solid.

note: The original says his cast is ninety and twelve. The rewrite says his pension and that he is twelve. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: My pension's ninety, and I'm twelve. Don't ask how. But we both have bad knees, at least.

note: The original says Amber was right that she is a terror at fights. The rewrite says she was right to be concerned.
last: As it turns out, she was entirely right to be concerned.

note: The original says the team fights to the worn pearl. The rewrite invents greater cohesion as the effect of a charm.
last: Charms, you say? Wear a pearl, and your team fights with greater cohesion. One pearl at a time. // Anything else?

note: Keep the game word charm. It is a term in this game.
last: (Press X, select Charm, and equip a pearl. Charms provide benefits to your entire team in battle.)

note: Amber is the keeper's name. The rewrite says "The amber".
last: The amber is the keeper. One hundred and three. Don't raise your voice at her. // She hears perfectly well and hates being shouted at.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: The Hilt road lies to the east, and the Shingle to the southeast. // Amber wishes to see you before anything else.

note: The original says the late ones (people whose shell has not come off) should get a go. The rewrite says those who came in late.
last: She says those who came in late deserve a turn. Here. Your turn.

note: The original says she shed the day she climbed down. The rewrite says she took it off and drops the game term shed. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: It's a Rider's cast, passed down from my grandmother's grandmother. // She took it off the very day she climbed down.

note: The original says the cast never fought. The rewrite says it never resisted.
last: It never resisted. It had walked a long way. It always wanted to go north.

note: Keep the game word conjoin. It is a term in this game.
last: Conjoined whorls are roaming free out here now. Two shells fused into one. Naturally!

note: The original says wild conjoined whorls are on the road. The rewrite says "wild patterns".
last: The road's covered in conjoined whorls now, wild patterns, two fused into one. // Never seen that before. Must be the moon.

note: The original asks if Ouro is the late one. The rewrite says "late arrival", which means someone who arrived late at the Pylon.
last: You're the... late arrival? From the Pylon?

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: The glass road lies to the southeast. The rule is the same. Secure the sword before the glass. // Quillon is quite adamant about this.

note: The choice to catch the moon with a horn becomes "Grab it" and drops the game term catch.
last: Grab it

note: The original says to duel with the moon sent out. The rewrite says to duel with that horn.
last: If you want to duel me, you'll have to do it with that horn. That's my condition.

note: The original means if the Seal lasts through the night. The rewrite says if it keeps the night out.
last: If it keeps the night out, then it stays. Then, breakfast.

note: Fall is a town name. The rewrite says "the Falls". Keep the name Fall.
last: Head south to the Falls, and unfortunately, you'll hit the incline next.

note: The original says keeper rematches are fought at level twenty-five. The rewrite says he fought at age twenty-five.
last: I fought at twenty-five. Everyone was. That's when talent showed.

note: The original says both teams fight at level 25. The rewrite says both players.
last: (You can challenge a keeper again after obtaining their pearl. Both players will fight at level 25.)

note: The original foretells that Ouro will have looked at its hands. The rewrite gives an order and says Ouro will look back on the moment.
last: You will go up. Look at its hands. You will look back on that moment.

note: The placeholder {#1} moves from the start of the line into the sentence as the thing Tack accepts.
last: I'll accept {#1}. I'm sticking with this star until you secure 1 victory.

note: The original challenges Ouro to a fight. The rewrite says try to argue.
last: 0 regrets. That's the count, alright? try to argue with that.

note: The original means Ouro coming up loose (their shell loosening). The rewrite says unprepared.
last: I'll take my post on the Climb. // If you show up unprepared, that adds 1 more Hermit to the mix, and I'm not accepting that.

note: The original tells Ouro to look back down. The rewrite adds "Keep moving" while Bare is blocking the way.
last: Glance downward. Keep moving.

note: The original says the fracture is a number of fingers long. The rewrite says fingers deep.
last: Your back is fractured {#1} fingers deep. I counted once, then again.

note: The original says Ouro is four spans tall and one span short of a Hand. The rewrite says four spans minus one hand's width.
last: You are as tall as four span-lengths, minus one hand's width.

note: The original says the air is close (muggy) in the room. The rewrite reads it as an order to pull in tight.
last: Pull in tight. A storm is rolling in for supper. It's going to rain inside. Rain in the soup.

note: The original says owe it all again. The rewrite says pay it back in full.
last: A Hand is worth eight pearls and a Climb. You've been carrying that debt. Now, pay it back in full.

note: The original says the Hands took orders from a habit (the cast at the post). The rewrite says they ran on autopilot.
last: We've been running on autopilot. Cheap habits. But we've owed full price for every single one.

note: The original says old shell and fractures. The rewrite says carcass and cracks and drops the game term fracture. Keep the game word fracture. It is a term in this game.
last: The Volute's old carcass rises and heads north, its towns mapped out in cracks.

note: Keep the name Sunday.
last: Tell them to come home on Sundays for soup.

note: The original says she said a new one. The rewrite says she said there is a new one.
last: Tell my little turnip she said there's a new one.

note: The original says the well's water is up to the top. The rewrite says the well is awake.
last: She's awake. Right at the top. She hasn't been scared in quite some time.

note: The original says they carry water from Rib. The rewrite says they haul the dust from Rib.
last: There's still dust. We haul it from Rib. It's a short trip. I still come to wait on her.

note: The original says one nail shed and its shell follows her. The rewrite says the nail fell off and drops shed. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: I bit my nails till one fell off. Its shell is clingy.

note: The original says the ship behaved in a seaworthy way. The rewrite says it conducts itself at sea.
last: Log. That is simply what a ship does. It conducts itself entirely at sea.

note: The original says the sea's cast. The rewrite says the sea's casting. Keep the game word cast. It is a term in this game.
last: The sea's casting. Gray, still, as tall as the weather.

note: The original says see you tomorrow and the roots too. The rewrite addresses "you two".
last: See you tomorrow, then. And you two as well.

note: The original has a notion under the bark. The rewrite says a thought forms and drops the game term notion. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: Beneath loose bark, a thought forms.

note: The original says Ouro keeps the bowl upside down. The rewrite says Ouro inverts it.
last: Ouro carefully inverts the bowl, catching the upward rain.

note: The original has a notion in the pouch. The rewrite says a trinket and drops the game term notion. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: Beneath a tilted blade lies a buckled pouch, containing a trinket and some cowrie shells.

note: The original says the soldier copies Ouro's steps the wrong way round. The rewrite says mirrors them but in reverse, which can read as the same way round and muddles the puzzle hint.
last: The soldier mirrors each of Ouro's steps in the opposite pen, but in reverse.

note: The original says he will not be the one to tell the swords. The rewrite says he won't pick one up.
last: The war ended before my gran was born. The swords never got the memo. I won't pick one up.

note: The original says the war horses have been whorls for a hundred years. The rewrite says idle and drops the game term whorl. Keep the game word whorl. It is a term in this game.
last: I brush the warhorses. They've been idle for a century but still love a good brush.

note: The original says "There I am" about her reflection. The rewrite says "Here I am".
last: Here I am! A bit muddy, but that's fine. Mud suits me.

note: The original says Ouro lit the glass room. The rewrite says Ouro shattered it.
last: You shattered the glass room! I heard it all the way from here.

note: The original says every Hand wears her glove and she has never shaken one. The rewrite says she gloves every hand and none are shaken, which is garbled.
last: I glove every hand. None are shaken. It's sad.

note: Purchase is the name of a Hand. The rewrite says "my Purchase".
last: I served as a Hand before my Purchase. I tended the groves. The Operculum sustained me. // Until it ceased.

note: The original says cutting one tree makes its neighbors shed. The rewrite says they drop their leaves, which changes the puzzle hint. Keep the game word shed. It is a term in this game.
last: Four have gone feral. Trim one, and the surrounding trees drop their leaves. // Such is the nature of the flora here.

note: The original says nobody drew the Blank into the map. The rewrite says nobody summoned it.
last: No one summoned me. Thus, I remain where I please. Today, that is here.

note: The original says the shell copies Ouro's steps the wrong way round. The rewrite says mirrors them but in reverse, which can read as the same way round and muddles the puzzle hint.
last: Old Amber's first shell mirrors each of Ouro's steps, but in reverse.

note: The leading comma becomes the literal text "[comma]".
last: [comma] hole filled

note: The original tells the turnip about soup. The rewrite sends love to "my little turnip soup".
last: Give my love to my little turnip soup.

note: Keep the name Sunday.
last: Tell them she's to be brought home on Sundays. Every single one.

note: The original means come home on Sundays without exception. The rewrite says it's Sunday. Keep the name Sundays.
last: Tell my little turnip it's Sunday, without fail.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Reach the eastern edge of the Margin.

note: The original asks who is turning Ouro's post. The rewrite asks who is keeping watch at it.
last: Stay seated for a minute before you leave. Who's keeping watch at your post while you're away?

note: The original says this seat shows what Ouro came out of. The rewrite says what brought Ouro here.
last: Come, sit. It's the best vantage point to see what brought you here.

note: The original says Cinch always taps his own foot in here. The rewrite asks Ouro to tap his foot.
last: Please tap my foot whenever you're in here. It's just a habit of mine.

note: The original says a tide bell turns the tide. The rewrite says it reverses the current.
last: (Ring the tide bell to reverse the current. At high tide, the exposed sand is submerged.)

note: The original says stars fall in a line at low tide. The rewrite says the stars align.
last: (At low tide, the sand is exposed, and stars align in a straight line.)

note: The original says a still shell is gone when the shadow passes. The rewrite says when its own shadow passes, which changes the rule.
last: (At low water, a shell that appears empty vanishes as its shadow passes.)

note: The original letter is addressed to the inside of the Volute. The rewrite says "Dear reader" and loses who she writes to.
last: Dear reader. The water is low. I'm sheltering in the log. These logs were once trees. // Dear trees, what is it like up there?

note: The original letter is addressed to the inside of the Volute. The rewrite says "Dear reader" and loses who she writes to.
last: Dear reader. Another one washed ashore today, hidden beneath a crab. The crab says hello.

note: The original says the family is inside the whelk because it is low water. The rewrite says they are good to go and loses that they are inside.
last: The tide is low, so we're good to go. Hi! No stopping now.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: I'm rocking, Dad.

note: The original says somebody finally read one of her letters. The rewrite begs someone to read one, which reverses it.
last: Dear whoever is inside. Please, someone read one. Someone actually read one.

note: The original says the writer is nobody here. The rewrite says nobody here knows them.
last: Dear whoever writes these. No one here knows them. We checked. Your letters are so huge.

note: The original says the Strandmonger keeps a shop counter in the east petal. The rewrite says he tracks a counter. Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: The Strandmonger tracks a counter located in the eastern petal.

note: The original warns against breaking the Sand Dollar to get at the doves. The rewrite says break the bank.
last: There are five doves down in the town square. Don't break the bank trying to catch them. // Folks have already tried.

note: The original says they came off the old shell. The rewrite says they arrived on it.
last: Our ancestors arrived on an old shell five generations ago. We walked the entire distance. // My feet still ache from it.

note: The original says your trader, meaning Ouro's Strandmonger. The rewrite says our trader.
last: Our trader buys our cowrie shells by the sack. We simply sweep them off the seaweed. // It's the easiest money you'll ever make.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: Don't sit still in a hollow shell when the tide is out. Obviously. Even the babies know that.

note: The original says cowries are cheap off the wrack, as cheap as sand. The rewrite says the wrack and the sand are cheap.
last: I make this trek twice a year for cowries. The wrack is cheap, and so is the sand.

note: The original says take her, meaning Small Gran. The rewrite says take it and swaps she to it.
last: Your gran said, "Tell my little turnip to take it." She said it to *them*, mind. Not to me.

note: The original says the road is worth more to Ouro than a cowrie and less to him. The rewrite compares it to a shell and is garbled. Keep the game word cowries. It is a term in this game.
last: I'll let it slide, just this once. // It's worth more to you than a shell is to me, so we both come out ahead. I come out aheader.

note: The original says thirty stars earns a notion. The rewrite says a thought and drops the game term notion. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: Catch thirty stars in a night, and you earn a thought. // Catch sixty, and you earn something truly unprecedented!!

note: The original says Tack came through Ouro's hole. The rewrite says it went through.
last: It went right through your 1 hole. Thanks for that.

note: The original says the cell holds a number of measures. The rewrite says that many were measured out.
last: {#1} measured out. {sack} remain in the sack.

note: The original says two of the Sifter's four whorls are salt. The rewrite says two of four components.
last: Two of my four components are salt, which overcomes both roots and beasts. Keep that in mind.

note: The original says the Sifter now has no house. The rewrite says the house is empty.
last: Just one house. According to my count, it's currently empty.

note: The original says the Sifter lost the house after two hours away. The rewrite says the Sifter gets two hours out of it and is garbled.
last: I've spent thirty years living there, yet I only get two hours out of it for a single grain. // It's a terrible trade.

note: The original says there is room at the fire until the Sifter finds another house. The rewrite says until he finds someone else.
last: Come sit by me. There's room at the fire until you find someone else.

note: The original says anything less than two lows will not do. The rewrite says if it moves any less, which is garbled.
last: It has to stay put for two consecutive lows. Two! If it moves any less, I won't trust it.

note: The original has a notion at the bottom. The rewrite says a thought takes shape and drops the game term notion. Keep the game word notion. It is a term in this game.
last: A razor hole, dug straight down. At the bottom, a thought takes shape.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: I stand in the gray at high tide. It's incredibly warm in there. Nobody believes me.

note: The original says you see only inside star rings and soft sand shows in a ring. The rewrite drops only and soft, which changes the rule. Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: (At low tide, the interior of landed star rings is visible, // while sand appears only as a surrounding ring.)

note: The original says a SALT whorl worn in the lead walks you through gray. The rewrite says worn smooth by the lead, which changes the rule.
last: (A SALT whorl, worn smooth by the lead, guides you through the gray.)

note: The original says Gloss is the keeper of the mouth. The rewrite says Gloss keeps the mouth shut.
last: Gloss keeps the mouth shut. The way down is past the blank, at the bottom of town.

note: The original says your reflection is three steps behind you. The rewrite says three steps behind mine.
last: Your reflection is three steps behind mine. Mine's four. I'm older, so.

note: The original says the spots are on the Cowrie's back and to catch one. The rewrite says the back porch and grab one. Keep the game word catch. It is a term in this game.
last: Put one on, and you'll be able to walk in it. They're on the back porch. Go grab one!

note: The original says the speaker sits in the only gap in town. The rewrite says the speaker is the only gap.
last: I dwell between the teeth. I'm the only gap in town, and I got here first.

note: The original means at every low water. The rewrite says at every low point.
last: At every low point, we stamp in unison. In unison, we stamp at every low point.

note: The original means the light came in at low water. The rewrite says at the low point.
last: The light entered at the low point, shining brilliantly! // Brilliantly, at the low point, the light entered!

note: The original says the light came in at low water. The rewrite says it trickled in low and slow.
last: The light trickled in, low and slow.

note: Keep the words written in capitals exactly as they are.
last: Everyone, stamp your feet!

note: The original says Cinch came down when the stamping started. The rewrite says it started.
last: Sit down. It started when the stamping began. I heard it from the bar.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: Swim back across the Flats to the Sand Dollar at high tide.

note: The original says when the tide rolls the Auger over. The rewrite says when the tide rolls in.
last: When the tide rolls in, the floor becomes the wall. You learn to sleep on both.

note: The original says pull the plug from the vent. The rewrite says disconnect the vent, which can read as closing it.
last: Disconnect vent {#1}

note: The original says plug the vent. The rewrite says connect the vent, which can read as opening it.
last: Connect vent {#1} ({#2} remaining)

note: The original says to sound the vents in that order. The rewrite says to chant the sequence.
last: The notches read four, two, four, one, four. Chant that sequence, and the tip will open.

note: The original names the point, the Auger's tip. The rewrite says the goal.
last: Higher. Keep going. The goal is up there. Only the small can fit. You're small.

note: Keep every direction exactly as the original says it.
last: Further down the shore, a line of hollows extends to the sea, // then curves eastward along the low-water mark.

note: The original says they will climb every low water. The rewrite says every rise.
last: Here. We have arrived. We are at the edge now, exactly where the Gleaner walks. // We will climb every single rise.

note: The original says the voice is heard on the sandbar and that this morning was seventy years ago. The rewrite says in the bar and makes it an anniversary.
last: This morning, I will hear that same voice in the bar. It will be exactly seventy years to the day.

note: The original says she takes off her boot on the sandbar. The rewrite says in the bar. Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: This morning, she will remove one boot in the bar to shake out the sand. The tide will be low.

note: The original says Tack is scratching the score in. The rewrite says scratching it, which can read as crossing it out.
last: {score}. That's over my 66. Fine. I'm scratching it.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: Now. Spring low. Four notches and a star.

note: Keep the game word low or high water. It is a term in this game.
last: A low spring tide.
